body: Claude: **suggestion**: Now that `lifetime` is cached alongside `until`, this one-sided gate can leave both stale and the schedule anchored to an expiry the cache no longer agrees with. A re-announcement carrying a shorter TTL (a different responder for the same shared PTR, or a responder that lowered its TTL) does shrink the cache entry, because `dns_cache_item_update_positive()` recomputes `until_valid` unconditionally from the new RR. But since the new `until` is smaller, `mdns_service_update()` is skipped, so the service keeps the older larger `until` plus the `lifetime` derived from it, and `mdns_maintenance_schedule()` then places the 80% point after the entry has actually been pruned: no maintenance query is sent before the record vanishes and the service silently drops off the browse list at the next unrelated revisit -- the same failure mode this commit fixes for the cap case, reached from the other direction. Gating on `service->until != until` would keep them in sync both ways; goodbyes are already excluded by the `rr->ttl <= 1` return just above, and a re-announcement with a larger TTL whose `until` is pinned by CACHE_TTL_MAX_USEC would then also correctly re-derive the (unchanged) lifetime rather than being ignored. Worth stating on the struct field too that `lifetime` may only be written together with `until`/`rr->ttl`.
